title: A look into my colony sim where every NPC has a memory, personality, and responds to anything - run automatically via local LLM
author: epochforgegame
selftext:
[Super excited about releasing my colony sim soon! ](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5062230/Epoch_Forge/)This clip is a few examples of what NPC dialogue is like - everything is grounded in real world facts, and what that NPC would actually know/think.

Let me know if you have any questions and wishlist if it looks interesting!

comments.author: dotoonly
comments.body: What do you mean by local llm. Meaning player has to connect local llm to it, or does it include one?

replies.author: epochforgegame
replies.body:
So the thing I'm super excited about with this game is that it does actually bundle with one. It uses Gemma E2B (https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B) which runs on <2GB RAM and I've tested it on a few of my own devices and it works well. I've spent a lot of time making sure the game and model work together rather than the model just making things up, so a lot of the model's job is choosing among prewritten prose. So the result is pretty cool. 

I do also have it so you can host a local model (LM Studio/Ollama, etc.) or connect to OpenRouter!

comments.author: ChemicalPresent8796
comments.body:
This looks interesting. The hard part we've run into with persistent NPCs is deciding which memories should still matter later.

Remembering every conversation is one thing. Knowing that a broken promise should affect how a character treats you weeks later is another.

How are you handling memory priority as the game gets longer? Are NPCs weighting memories by how much they change relationships or decisions, or mainly retrieving relevant past conversations?
